cover.prompt: American comic book horror cover, painted in 1970s EC Comics / Creepy magazine style, full color, grotesque and eerie but non-violent. A tall bathroom mirror mounted on a peeling olive-green wallpaper, the mirror surface foggy. In the reflection, a pale woman who does NOT match the figure seen from behind. A single thin pale hand reaches out from inside the mirror, fingers pressing against the glass from behind. From the back of the real figure in the foreground, we see a woman with shoulder-length dark brown hair in a yellow sweater, standing close to the mirror with her back to the viewer. The word "REFLECTION" is at the top in classic comic horror hand-lettering, but the letter "O" is replaced by a cracked mirror reflection, and small moth-wing shapes orbit the title. Moody bathroom with dim warm bulb light, dramatic black shadows, heavy black inking, Ben-Day dots texture, high contrast saturated desaturated palette (mustard yellow, olive green, dusty pink, deep brown). Single full-page splash composition. Clean hand-lettered English title text, render text exactly as quoted.

p1.prompt: American horror comic page in 1970s EC Comics / Creepy magazine style, full color, two panels, eerie and grotesque but non-violent. Panel 1 (wide): a tired young woman in her 30s with shoulder-length dark brown hair wearing a mustard sweater and jeans carries a cardboard moving box into an old apartment hallway with peeling olive wallpaper, single bare bulb overhead, heavy shadows, her face half in shadow. Caption box at top: "Day 1. The new apartment." Panel 2: she stands in front of a foggy bathroom mirror, holding her toothbrush, looking at her own reflection, mid-yawn, a small half-smile. In the mirror, her reflection wears the SAME clothes but its smile is fractionally wider and slightly delayed, like it copied her a second too late. A tiny moth flies near the mirror frame. Clean white speech bubble from Mira: "Hm. Tired already." Caption box at bottom: "The smile came back wrong." Heavy black inking, Ben-Day dots, high contrast muted palette (mustard, olive, dusty rose, deep brown), dramatic shadows. Render text exactly as quoted.

p2.prompt: American horror comic page in 1970s EC Comics / Creepy magazine style, full color, two panels, eerie and grotesque but non-violent. Panel 1: late night exterior establishing shot — a window of an apartment building glowing sickly yellow against a dark blue night sky with a thin crescent moon, moths circling the window light. Panel 2 (large): the same bathroom as before, the young woman with dark brown hair and mustard sweater stands in front of the bathroom mirror at 3 AM, exhausted, face neutral and tired, NOT smiling. In the mirror, her reflection wears the same clothes but its face is set in a soft, calm, deliberate smile — eyes wide open and watching. A thin moth sits on the mirror frame. Speech bubble from the reflection, but tagged with a different visual style (smaller, italic caption): "Why so tired, Mira?" Speech bubble from Mira in the real world, with a small confused sweat drop: "…I didn't say anything." Caption box: "Day 7. It smiled first." Heavy black inking, Ben-Day dots, high contrast, dramatic shadows. Render text exactly as quoted.

p3.prompt: American horror comic page in 1970s EC Comics / Creepy magazine style, full color, three panels, eerie and grotesque but non-violent. p4.prompt: American horror comic page in 1970s EC Comics / Creepy magazine style, full color, exactly two panels, eerie and grotesque but non-violent. Panel 1 (wide): the bathroom at night, every light off except a thin strip of moonlight. Mira with dark brown hair in a white t-shirt stands very close to the mirror, both palms pressed flat against the glass from the outside, mouth open in shock, eyes wide. In the mirror, her reflection is no longer a reflection — it is a thin pale figure pressed against the glass from the INSIDE, hands mirroring Mira's but wearing the 1940s high-collar teal dress, its soft smile gone, mouth a flat line, eyes locked on Mira. Caption box at top of this panel: "Day 21. She spoke at last." Panel 2: extreme close-up of the glass surface from Mira's side. On the inner side of the mirror, in condensation, a single line of handwriting: "When did you move in?" A moth's wing is pressed against the glass beside the writing. Mira's speech bubble, tiny and cracked: "…out." Caption box at bottom of this panel: "THE END." Heavy black inking, Ben-Day dots, dramatic shadows, sickly yellow-green palette. Render each caption box and each speech bubble exactly once, render text exactly as quoted, do not duplicate any text.
